questionText: Which of the following are core components of Google Cloud Pub/Sub?

answers.text: Topics
Subscriptions
Queues
Exchanges
Channels

questionText: What are the primary benefits of using Google Cloud Pub/Sub?

answers.text: Asynchronous messaging
Decoupling of services
Synchronous communication
Tight service coupling
Real-time data streaming to a single client

questionText: Which of the following describe the function of a Pub/Sub topic?

answers.text: A named resource to which messages are sent.
A channel for receiving messages.
A resource that allows subscribers to receive messages.
A logical access point to the Pub/Sub messaging system.
A storage mechanism for message history.

questionText: What is a Pub/Sub subscription?

answers.text: A configuration that defines how messages are delivered to subscribers.
A set of rules for filtering messages.
A push configuration for message delivery.
A pull configuration for message delivery.
A named resource representing an interest in receiving messages from a specific topic.

questionText: How can messages be delivered from Pub/Sub to subscribers?

answers.text: Push delivery
Pull delivery
Direct method invocation
HTTP GET requests
Message queuing within the subscriber application

questionText: What is message acknowledgment in Pub/Sub?

answers.text: A mechanism for subscribers to confirm successful message processing.
A signal to Pub/Sub that a message can be deleted.
A way to reorder messages.
A method for publishers to verify message receipt.
A process to increase message priority.

questionText: What happens if a subscriber fails to acknowledge a message within the acknowledgment deadline?

answers.text: The message is redelivered to another subscriber (or the same subscriber).
The message is considered unacknowledged.
The message is permanently deleted.
The subscriber's IP address is blacklisted.
The acknowledgment deadline is automatically extended indefinitely.

questionText: Which of the following are valid attributes for Pub/Sub messages?

answers.text: Key-value pairs
Metadata for message filtering and routing
Binary payloads
Message sequencing numbers
JSON objects only

questionText: What is the maximum message size for Google Cloud Pub/Sub?

answers.text: 10 MB
10 MiB
1 MB
100 MB
1 GB

Editor (if granted on the project)
Pub/Sub Subscriber

questionText: Which IAM roles are commonly used for subscribing to Pub/Sub messages?

answers.text: Pub/Sub Subscriber
Viewer (if granted on the project)

questionText: What is the purpose of message filtering in Pub/Sub subscriptions?

answers.text: To receive only messages that match specific attribute criteria.
To reduce the number of messages processed by the subscriber.
To modify the message payload before delivery.
To prioritize messages for delivery.
To ensure exactly-once processing.

questionText: What is a Dead Letter Topic in Pub/Sub?

answers.text: A topic to which unacknowledged messages are sent after exceeding a retry policy.
A topic used for debugging message delivery failures.
A topic that receives all messages published to the original topic.
A topic that automatically acknowledges all messages.
A topic that stores only successfully processed messages.

questionText: Which of the following are common use cases for Google Cloud Pub/Sub?

answers.text: Event ingestion and processing
Distributed system integration
Synchronous API calls
Real-time website analytics aggregation
Direct database querying

questionText: What is message ordering in Pub/Sub?

answers.text: Ensures that messages with the same ordering key are delivered in the order they were published.
A feature that requires specific configuration on the subscription.
Guarantees global message order across all topics.
Applies ordering to all messages by default.
Requires a unique ordering key for every message.

questionText: What is the role of the 'Editor' role in Pub/Sub?

answers.text: Allows full management of Pub/Sub resources, including creating, deleting, and modifying topics and subscriptions.
Grants permissions to publish and subscribe to messages.
Grants broad permissions across GCP resources, which may include Pub/Sub.
Only allows viewing Pub/Sub configurations.
Grants permission to only acknowledge messages.

questionText: How can you monitor Pub/Sub usage and performance?

answers.text: Using Cloud Monitoring metrics.
Viewing logs in Cloud Logging.
Checking the Pub/Sub console dashboard for error codes.
Implementing custom heartbeat signals from subscribers.
Analyzing BigQuery audit logs for message throughput.

questionText: What is the purpose of the `ackId` in Pub/Sub pull subscriptions?

answers.text: It's a unique identifier for a message that must be used to acknowledge it.
It's used by Pub/Sub to track which messages have been delivered.
It's a timestamp of when the message was published.
It's a unique identifier for the subscriber.
It's a flag to indicate message priority.

questionText: Which of the following are considered managed services that integrate well with Pub/Sub?

answers.text: Cloud Functions
Cloud Run

questionText: What is the retention period for unacknowledged messages in Pub/Sub?

answers.text: Messages are retained for a default period of 7 days.
The retention period can be configured up to 7 days for the subscription.
Messages are retained indefinitely until acknowledged.
Messages are retained for a maximum of 24 hours.
Messages are deleted immediately if not acknowledged within 60 seconds.

questionText: What is a 'snapshot' in Pub/Sub?

answers.text: A named resource that stores the state of a subscription at a specific point in time.
A way to replay messages from a subscription.
A copy of the topic's entire message history.
A mechanism for archiving messages permanently.
A type of subscriber that only receives messages once.

questionText: Which of the following are key characteristics of Pub/Sub's publish-subscribe model?

answers.text: Decoupling of publishers and subscribers.
Scalability and high availability.
Tight coupling between services.
Synchronous message delivery.
Guaranteed in-order delivery without ordering keys.

questionText: What is the maximum number of Pub/Sub topics allowed per project?

answers.text: The default limit is 10,000 topics per project.
This limit can be increased by requesting a quota increase.
There is no limit to the number of topics.
The default limit is 1,000 topics per project.
The limit is 100 topics per project.

questionText: What is the maximum number of subscriptions allowed per topic?

answers.text: The default limit is 10,000 subscriptions per topic.
This limit can be increased by requesting a quota increase.
There is no limit to the number of subscriptions.

questionText: What is the purpose of a 'retry policy' for Pub/Sub subscriptions?

answers.text: To configure how many times Pub/Sub should attempt to redeliver a message.
To define a time duration after which Pub/Sub will stop retrying delivery.
To enable immediate redelivery of all failed messages.
To specify which subscribers should receive retried messages.
To control the size of messages that are retried.
